About The Team

The ML API Quality team is responsible for the confidence behind every production release shipped to Cerebras Inference Cloud. We work closely with platform, infrastructure, ML systems, and product engineering teams to ensure that rapid iteration never comes at the expense of customer trust. Our environment spans distributed cloud systems, multi-region deployments, APIs, orchestration layers, and hardware-backed inference services.

We are scaling quickly. The systems are growing in complexity, traffic is increasing rapidly, and release velocity remains high. We need engineers who can build quality systems that scale with the business.

About The Role

As a Senior Software Engineer in Test for the ML API features team, you will lead testing strategy and execution for AI/ML models, evaluating accuracy, fairness, and performance at scale. You will serve as a key technical leader in delivering and validating all software and hardware components for Cerebras API Features. You will own software components feature integration quality and drive pre-deployment and production validation for Cerebras inference solutions. In this role, you will define and champion best testing practices, establish robust debugging methodologies, and mentor junior engineers while advocating for world-class product quality.

Responsibilities

 - Architect and own end-to-end test strategies for new features, developing scalable tests, frameworks, and tooling to ensure quality.

 - Lead contributions to industry-standard benchmarks and drive adoption of rigorous evaluation methodologies.

 - Define and drive automation initiatives to significantly improve internal engineering efficiency and test coverage.

 - Make strategic decisions around coverage trade-offs, resource requirements, and risk-based testing priorities.

 - Serve as a technical anchor in a highly agile environment, adapting quickly to shifting priorities while maintaining quality standards.

 - Mentor and guide junior SDETs on testing methodology, debugging practices, and automation development.

 - Proactively identify systemic quality gaps and drive cross-functional initiatives to address them.

 - Lead and facilitate effective technical communication across teams and time zones.

Skills & Qualifications

 - 5+ years of relevant industry experience in software integration, development, or quality engineering.

 - Deep expertise in automation and programming using one or more languages such as Python, C++, or Go; ability to design and build reusable test frameworks from the ground up.

 - Proven experience testing compute, machine learning, networking, or storage systems within large-scale enterprise environments.

 - Strong track record of debugging complex issues across distributed, scaled-out deployments.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional quality initiatives involving product development, product management, customer operations, and field teams.

 - Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with experience presenting technical findings to both engineering and leadership audiences.

 - Strong organizational skills, ownership mindset, and ability to drive projects to completion independently.

 - Experience leading and mentoring engineers across geographically dispersed teams and time zones.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications

 - Hands-on experience with ML workloads including LLM and/or multimodal training or inference.

 - Deep familiarity with hardware architecture, performance optimizations, compilers, and ML frameworks.

 - Experience designing test strategies for distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and security validation.

 - Experience with microservices deployment, debugging, and orchestration at scale.

 - Prior experience owning or significantly contributing to a team's quality engineering culture or test infrastructure.

Location

This role follows a hybrid schedule, requiring in-office presence 3 days per week. Fully remote is not an option.

Office locations: Sunnyvale, CA | Toronto, Canada

About the Role

Cerebras is building a new generation of disaggregated AI inference systems that combine GPU-accelerated prefill with ultra-fast decode on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine.

We are hiring a Software Engineer to build and evolve the ML API layer that makes this heterogeneous serving system accessible, reliable, and easy to use. You will work across our inference APIs, model integration layer, request-routing services and Cerebras inference platform to deliver a consistent experience across models and accelerator backends.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning systems, API design, model serving, and distributed systems. You will enable new model architectures and inference capabilities, define stable user-facing behavior, and ensure that features such as streaming, sampling, tool use, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and model configuration behave correctly and consistently in production.

You will work closely with model enablement, compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, product, customer-facing teams, and customers directly. This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys turning rapidly evolving ML capabilities into durable, production-quality APIs.

Responsibilities

 - Build production ML inference APIs. Design, implement, and maintain APIs for chat completions, text generation, streaming, model configuration, tool calling, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and other emerging inference capabilities.

 - Deliver a unified serving experience. Create consistent request and response semantics across GPU prefill, Cerebras decode, and other heterogeneous inference backends.

 - Enable new models and capabilities. Integrate emerging foundation models, tokenizers, prompt formats, sampling methods, attention variants, multimodal inputs, and model-specific features into the serving platform.

 - Own API compatibility and evolution. Maintain compatibility with widely adopted inference interfaces while designing Cerebras-specific extensions. Establish clear versioning, deprecation, validation, and backward compatibility practices.

 - Integrate with model-serving runtimes. Extend and integrate custom inference services with vLLM, PyTorch, Hugging Face libraries, the AMD ROCm stack, and Cerebras runtime components.

 - Support disaggregated inference. Build the control and data paths required to coordinate GPU prefill with Cerebras decode, including request routing, state transfer, error handling, retries, and lifecycle management.

 - Improve serving performance. Optimize streaming behavior, time to first token, request latency, throughput, batching, serialization, tokenization, scheduling, and communication between serving components.

 - Ensure functional and numerical correctness. Build validation systems for tokenization, sampling, logits, generated outputs, precision changes, model upgrades, determinism, and compatibility across serving backends.

 - Strengthen reliability and observability. Define end-to-end service indicators and build structured logging, tracing, metrics, dashboards, health checks, and diagnostic tooling for production inference traffic.

 - Develop testing and qualification infrastructure. Create conformance tests, workload-replay tools, model-validation suites, performance benchmarks, integration tests, and release gates.

 - Improve developer experience. Build intuitive configuration, SDKs, documentation, examples, debugging tools, and self-service workflows for internal developers, customers, and partners.

 - Collaborate across the stack. Partner with compiler, runtime, kernel, cloud, product, and solutions teams to translate model and customer requirements into scalable serving capabilities.

Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience, including substantial individual-contributor ownership of production software or distributed systems.

 - Strong programming ability in Python and Go plus experience developing performance-sensitive or highly concurrent services in C++, Rust, or a similar systems language.

 - Experience building stable APIs with clear validation, error handling, observability, compatibility, and versioning practices. 

 - Experience integrating software across service, framework, runtime, and infrastructure boundaries.

 - Experience designing or maintaining OpenAI-compatible, gRPC, REST, or streaming inference APIs. 

 - Experience with Linux, containers, Kubernetes or comparable orchestration systems, CI/CD, and operating latency-sensitive services in production.

 - Ability to diagnose correctness, reliability, and performance issues across multiple components of a distributed serving system.

 - Strong communication and cross-functional execution skills, with the ability to turn ambiguous model or product requirements into production-quality software.

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience modifying or contributing to vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Triton, TensorRT-LLM, or another open-source ML systems project.

 - Experience creating API conformance, model-quality, numerical-comparison, determinism, or performance-regression test systems

 - Experience building SDKs, developer tools, model registries, configuration systems, or self-service ML platforms.

 - Experience with multi-model or multi-tenant inference platforms, including routing, admission control, fairness, quotas, rate limiting, and capacity-aware scheduling

 - Understanding of model-specific tokenization, chat templates, generation configuration, logits processing, stopping criteria, tool calling, structured generation, and constrained decoding.

 - Experience with disaggregated prefill/decode architectures, KV-cache transfer, prefix caching, chunked prefill, memory-aware admission control, or request scheduling.

 - Experience designing, building, or operating production APIs and services for machine learning, large language models, or other data-intensive applications. 

 - Familiarity with reduced-precision inference and quantization formats such as BF16, FP8, FP4, INT8, or INT4.

Why Join Cerebras

Put your accounting expertise to work. Help shape what comes next. 
 At Acuity Insights, we’re strengthening our accounting operations, improving our systems, and finding better ways to work. We’re looking for an experienced accountant who can take on complex work independently and help us build a stronger, more effective accounting function.
 As our Senior Accountant, you’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, from close and financial reporting to revenue, reconciliations, and audit readiness. You’ll also help strengthen the accuracy and reliability of our financial and business reporting, including recurring revenue metrics, while contributing accounting insights to budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
 You’ll work closely with our Controller and alongside a small accounting team, bringing the judgment to work through complex accounting questions, identify root causes, and see issues through to resolution. Your experience will also help strengthen the team through shared knowledge, guidance, and better ways of working.
 There’s plenty to improve and build. We’re preparing for a new accounting system, exploring automation and AI, and reducing the manual work that slows us down. You’ll have the opportunity to lead meaningful improvements while helping make our accounting processes more reliable and scalable.
 If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, sharing what you know, and finding better ways to get things done, there’s a lot here for you to contribute.
 Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. You’re welcome to use AI thoughtfully when preparing your application and conversations with our team. Just make sure what you share reflects your own experience, thinking, and judgment. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.
 We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.
 Own complex accounting work 
 You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.
 When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.
 Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting 
 You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.
 You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..
 Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight 
 You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.
 You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.
 Help modernize our accounting systems 
 We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.
 Improve how Accounting works 
 You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.
 You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.
 The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.
 Who You’ll Work With and How
 You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:
 Your Accounting teammates , to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
 Revenue Operations , to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.
 People & Culture , on payroll, employee-related accounting, and the processes that connect our teams.
 Leaders and budget owners , to understand the context behind transactions, resolve accounting questions, and support reliable financial information.
 External partners , including auditors and other Finance partners, to support reporting, compliance, and audit readiness.
 You’ll work with a high degree of independence, but not in isolation. You’ll know when to make decisions, when to bring others in, and how to build trust through clear communication, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first three months, you’ll build an understanding of Acuity’s business, accounting cycle, systems, and controls. You’ll begin taking ownership of key accounting responsibilities, building relationships across the business, and identifying opportunities to improve how work gets done.
 By six months, you’ll independently own significant areas of the accounting cycle, confidently work through complex reconciliations and accounting questions, and identify issues before they become problems. You’ll also begin turning improvement opportunities into practical changes.
 By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted source of accounting expertise, handling complex work with minimal guidance and contributing improvements beyond your own responsibilities. Your impact will be visible in stronger processes, better controls, and greater shared knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 How You’ll Succeed
 You’ll likely thrive here if you:
 Take ownership. You follow work through to resolution, surface issues early, and take responsibility for accurate, reliable outcomes.
 Look beyond the numbers. You investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and connect the dots to understand what’s really happening.
 Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
 Look for better ways of working. Y ou notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
 Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 Use technology thoughtfully. You explore how systems, automation, and AI can improve your work, applying the same judgment and care you’d bring to any accounting decision.
 Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 As the Finance function evolves, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on broader ownership, and contribute to larger systems and process improvements.
 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:
 Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.
 Preparing or supporting financial reporting, ensuring the underlying accounting records are accurate, complete, and well supported.
 Working across revenue recognition, invoicing, receivables, or other core accounting activities, with an understanding of how they connect through the accounting cycle.
 Investigating complex accounting questions and discrepancies, applying accounting principles and professional judgment to determine the right path forward.
 Supporting external audits and maintaining strong documentation, controls, and audit readiness.
 Improving accounting processes, workflows, or systems to reduce manual work, strengthen reliability, and make the work more efficient.
 Working independently in evolving environments, knowing when to make decisions, collaborate, or escalate.
 Additional experience that would be valuable: Recurring revenue reporting, deferred revenue, budgeting, forecasting, cash management, or accounting system implementations.
 Our current Finance systems include Xero, Dext, Airwallex, Plooto, and Stripe. You don’t need experience with these specific tools, but you should be comfortable working with cloud-based accounting systems and learning new technology.
 A CPA designation, or progress toward one, is an asset but not required. Equivalent expertise developed through experience is equally valued.
 How We Support You
 Transparent compensation. A salary between $95,000 - $105,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
 Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening your accounting expertise, building new technical skills, or exploring new areas of interest.
 Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.
 Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
 Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
 Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
 Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.
 Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.
 What Happens After You Apply
 We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.
 We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some interviews, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.
 Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you. 
 Steps in the Process 
 Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision. 
 Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
 Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.
 Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Controller to explore the accounting work you’ve owned, how you approach complex problems, and the decisions you’ve made along the way. If you have an example of real work you’re proud of and can share, bring it along. It could be a process you’ve improved or a way you’ve used technology, automation, or AI to work more effectively. No need to prepare anything new or formal. It’s an opportunity to share how you approached the work, the judgment you applied, and what you learned.
 Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and improve ways of working, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done.
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team.
 Opportunities to share ideas and perspectives that help inform our direction.
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise, challenge thinking, and learn from one another.
 A culture of curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful experimentation, including how we use AI.
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness.
 As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions, challenge assumptions, and contribute to work that matters.
 About Acuity Insights
 At Acuity Insights, we build research-backed technology that helps higher education institutions better understand people, make informed decisions, and support learner development.
 We believe people are more than their grades, and that human potential can be understood, nurtured, and developed throughout the educational journey.
 Our products support institutions and learners at different stages, from identifying potential and making fairer admissions decisions to supporting education, professional development, and growth. Our Casper situational judgment test, developed by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.
 Today, we’re building toward a more connected ecosystem that brings together assessment, education, and development. By combining research, technology, and responsible AI, we aim to help institutions make better decisions, create more meaningful learning experiences, and support people in reaching their potential.
 We’re at a point in our evolution where the work we do today is helping shape what’s possible tomorrow. And the people who join us will have an opportunity to contribute to that future.

 Pipeline generation and conversion

In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.
 Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.
 Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.

 Build a personal banking experience so good that people tell their friends and colleagues about it

 Drive the use of AI in products where it makes the experience meaningfully better

 Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, including how personal banking connects to the businesses Mercury already serves
 Make reliability and trust product features: own uptime, correctness, latency, and support outcomes, and be measured on them
 Align the ecosystem: bring product, engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive strategy

 A consumer product leader with taste: you have built products millions of people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
 You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
 An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation-oriented approach

 At Treewalk, you'll run the day-to-day finance engine for the Indigenous governments, organizations and businesses we serve: clean books, a disciplined month-end close, timely funder reporting and year-end files that sail through audit. You'll own a portfolio of clients, acting as their fractional controller. We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Management to build and lead the operating infrastructure required to bring our products to market, scale them globally, and support them throughout their lifecycle. This role sits within the Supply Chain organization and reports to the Sr. Director, Operations & Strategic Partnerships. This role has high exposure to CEO level decisions and engagement and demonstrated leadership experience is a requirement.
 This is a builder role within the Supply Chain. You will own the Supply Chain deliverables covering our cross functional go to market and customer engagement. This includes driving product certifications and market readiness, enhancing RMA and customer satisfaction processes, as well as driving our Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Your job is to establish clear ownership, build scalable processes, develop the team, and create the operating mechanisms required to support a rapidly growing hardware business, working in close partnership with the other functions needed to achieve these goals.
 We are not looking for someone to administer existing processes. We are looking for someone who sees ambiguity, creates structure, drives decisions, and most importantly takes end-to-end ownership. Your mandate is simple: build it, own it, and scale it.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON; Austin, TX; or Santa Clara, CA. 
 Who You Are 
 A builder who is comfortable entering an environment where processes and ownership are not fully defined, then turning ambiguity into a clear operating model and an executable plan.
 An experienced hardware and supply chain operator who understands how Engineering, Product, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Legal, and customer teams connect across the product lifecycle.
 A cross-functional leader who can align senior stakeholders, establish decision rights, and drive accountability without waiting for someone else to define ownership.
 A data-driven and analytically rigorous decision-maker who can make sound judgments with incomplete information and maintain urgency through execution.
 A people leader who develops strong teams, builds subject matter expertise, and creates a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.
 What We Need 
 Drive cross-functional processes and own Supply Chain deliverables for global product certification and market readiness, including certification roadmaps across products and countries, clear readiness gates, coordination with Engineering, Product, Legal, manufacturing partners, test labs, and regulatory bodies, and early mitigation of risks that could affect customer commitments or launches.
 Own and mature the company’s S&OP process by connecting customer demand, Sales forecasts, supply, manufacturing capacity, inventory, and financial objectives into a disciplined operating cadence and trusted view for executive decision-making.
 Build and own the end-to-end global RMA and customer operations model within Supply Chain, covering intake, triage, replacement, repair, warranty management, disposition, customer communication, service levels, escalation paths, and performance metrics, in partnership with Customer, Quality, and Engineering teams.
 Establish the processes, systems, KPIs, dashboards, governance, and operating mechanisms required to scale, including measures for forecast accuracy, supply performance, inventory health, backlog, certification readiness, RMA performance, and execution against plan.
 Lead cross-functional execution with Sales, Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, test labs, regulatory bodies, and customer teams. Establish clear decision rights, simplify complex workflows, identify gaps before they become business problems, and drive shared decisions through to completion while retaining Supply Chain ownership of the deliverables.
 What You Will Learn 
 Gain broad exposure to the full operating model of a rapidly growing hardware and semiconductor business, from product development and global market readiness through supply planning, manufacturing, delivery, and customer support.
 Build expertise in integrating Supply Chain-owned certification deliverables, S&OP, RMA, and customer operations into one scalable product lifecycle operating system.
 Develop the leadership and operating mechanisms required to turn cross-functional complexity into clear ownership, timely decisions, and measurable execution.
 See directly how operational decisions influence product launch timing, customer commitments, product quality, inventory, revenue, and the company’s ability to scale globally.
 Create the foundation for a supply chain management organization that grows with Tenstorrent’s products, markets, customers, and operational complexity.
 Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The duties and responsibilities of the Press Operator are detailed below, but not limited to the following:
 Efficiently operate the extrusion press while maintaining good quality that meets Almag’s quality standards. 
 Keep track of equipment performance and ensure press is well tuned, and temperatures are being properly managed from billet oven to press exit temperatures.
 Responsible for monitoring runout efficiency such as length, speed, and finish.
 Reference work orders to ensure press is running at the optimal speeds to maximize productivity.
 Ensure billet zone temperatures are setup, monitored and maintained throughout the runs. Mark extrusions accordingly if temperatures do not meet requirements.
 Die management - Ensure all necessary tooling is available at the beginning and throughout shift.
 Load dies into press and ensure presses are not waiting for die changes. Importance must be given to ensure dies are not loaded too early or too late.
 Ensure die temperatures are maintained when dies are loaded and removed from the ovens.
 Responsible for communicating directly with the team leads/maintenance team if any mechanical breakdowns or issues are encountered.

 Ensure average speeds are followed based on information contained on work orders. If deviations occur, ensure note is made in EPICS and Team Lead is notified.
 Responsible for EPICS entries for billet lengths, cut offs, cut sizes, etc., and highlight any special notes and instructions that the team needs to focus on. 
 Responsible for entering all downtime, die fails, quality issues, and schedule adherence notes in EPICS.
 Responsible for checking notes in EPICS and viewing drawings throughout the shift to ensure work orders are followed correctly.
 Responsible for checking the run out on the second billet produced. Report to Team Lead if billet length scheduled is inappropriate and have it changed to improve yield.
 Ensure sufficient spacing is kept between extrusion pieces on the cooling table to make sure proper cooling is maintained.
 Responsible for ensuring the extrusion is correctly fed into puller jaws. Notify maintenance/team lead if any issues occur.
 Ensure exit/runout temperatures are monitored and maintained throughout the run. 
 Maintain quality checks at front end of press during operation and continuously throughout the shift.
 Press samples must be properly labelled and kept together for traceability
 Ensure samples are taken after the first billet and verify dimensions and surface finish according to drawings in EPICS.
 Ensure all billets and alloys used are accounted for in EPICS and documented accurately.
 Check finish and dimensions on extrusions at the required frequency.
 Complete press Ascona scans as required.
 Must have knowledge and ability to operate all equipment at saw and stretcher.
 Other duties as assigned.

 High school Diploma with some technical background and mechanical aptitude.
 Extrusion experience is an asset.

 1-2 years’ experience in an industrial environment.
 Knowledge of machinery and ability to read drawings is an asset. Willing to train.  
 Must be willing and able to train and develop as a saw operator / inspector, stretcher operator and die preparation operator as understating these jobs and their impact is critical to developing as a competent press operator.
 Basic computer skills including MS Windows is required. Other MS software is an asset. 
 Understanding of measurements, tolerances, basic geometry, and numeracy comprehension.

To advance technology adoption in the construction industry by delivering efficiency, visibility, and communication at scale.

veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is seeking an Product Marketing Manager to own the commercialization of our restoration portfolio: turning every project we plant into a sales-ready package, and acting as the technical and impact expert our revenue teams bring into the room.
 We have active restoration projects across the globe, each one carries real depth, identifying the purpose behind the site, whether the trees are permanent or on a managed harvest rotation, the species mix and why it was chosen, survivability and monitoring data, the workers and communities involved, and the ecosystem returning around it. We need someone who can translate project details into one canonical source of truth, packaging it into narratives, value propositions, and assets our Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success teams can actually use, and then standing behind it on live calls.
 This role is a deliberate blend of product marketing, product ownership, and sales enablement. You will own the story of what we sell, not the marketing gloss, but the substantive, verifiable, layered version that wins enterprise deals. This is a storyteller's role first. You will be fluent enough in forestry, permanence, survivability, and our on-site technology to hold your own with a sustainability lead or a diligence team, but the reason we're hiring is narrative craft: the ability to make a Fortune 500 buyer feel what changes for a worker who once felled trees for income and now earns more, more securely, planting them.
 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)
 Source of truth, live and trusted. One canonical project library covering 100% of active projects — purpose, permanence and harvest model, species mix, survivability, monitoring methodology, workforce and community context, ecosystem outcomes — current, maintained on an agreed cadence with Forest, and surfaced in internal materials for live call support.
 Every project sales-ready. A sales-ready package shipped for every active project: positioning, value proposition, proof points, pricing guidance, and customer-facing assets. No rep builds their own version from scratch.
 Impact story, three layers deep. A worker, community, and ecosystem narrative built and evidenced for our priority projects, backed by real data and media from veritree's technology — credible enough to survive diligence, specific enough to be memorable, and never greenwashing.
 Enablement that changes rep behaviour. Playbooks, proof-point libraries, objection handling, and training delivered so every Account Executive, Business Development Rep, and Customer Success Manager tells the same story, with adoption measured through call reviews and certification rather than assumed.
 Launch discipline. A cross-functional launch checklist and readiness standard, owned by you and adopted across Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, so nothing goes to market half-built.
 What You'll Do
 Source of Truth & Project Intelligence 
 You will build and own veritree's canonical library of project facts — one current, authoritative reference for every project we sell, replacing the scattered documents and tribal knowledge in use today.
 You will work directly with the Forest team to turn their intake into commercially usable intelligence: project purpose, permanence versus managed harvest and rotation length, species selection and rationale, survivability and mortality data, monitoring methodology, and site-level context.
 You will keep it current, with a defined maintenance cadence, clear ownership of each input, and version control the rest of the business can rely on.
 You will make it accessible where our teams actually work, surfacing project facts in Forge and our AI tooling so a rep can get an accurate answer during a live call, not after it.
 Packaging, Positioning & Pricing 
 You will translate every project into a sales-ready package: the narrative, the value proposition, the proof points, and the per-project assets that make it sellable.
 You will standardize delivery into ecosystem packages — mangrove, terrestrial, wildfire, agroforestry — rather than rebuild bespoke every deal, and you will own the product catalogue.
 You will own positioning across our growing solution portfolio, so that as we move from selling a single product toward solution-selling across multiple offerings and stakeholders, the story stays coherent.
 You will partner with Revenue and Finance on per-project pricing guidance and the commercial logic behind it, ensuring reps understand not just the price but why the project is worth it.
 You will own the change-flow when a metric is updated. When survivability, planting hours, or carbon updates, you push the correction into collateral, the portal, and CS on a set cadence — and you audit what's already in market.
 You will define which projects we lead with for which segments, and build the matching logic that helps reps put the right project in front of the right buyer.
 Impact Storytelling 
 You will build the impact narrative at three layers, and go deeper than the category norm on each:
 The worker — what this work actually changes for the individual, including the person who once cut and sold timber to feed their family and now earns better, more secure income restoring the same landscape.
 The community — how stable, better-paying restoration work compounds into local economic resilience, and what that looks like in the specific communities we operate in.
 The ecosystem — what returns to the site: canopy, soil, water, birds, wildlife, biodiversity — and how our technology measures and verifies it.
 You will ground every layer in evidence, using veritree's existing monitoring technology, field data, and media to turn claims into proof our clients can publish and defend.
 You will partner with Marketing to convert that depth into case studies, impact reports, campaign material, and event content.
 Sales Enablement 
 You will turn Forest's methodologies into sales-ready material — survivability, planting hours, social impact, carbon, permanence, verification — as defensible talk tracks, proof points, and objection handling. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one, and you only ever ship the defensible one.
 You will own the enablement library for project and impact content: playbooks, proof points, objection handling, discovery guidance, and competitive framing.
 You will design and deliver training and certification so every rep across Business Development, Sales, and Customer Success can tell the story consistently and credibly.
 You will review calls, identify where the story is breaking down, and close the gap with better material and better coaching rather than more documents.
 You will run a feedback loop from the field back into packaging, so what we ship next reflects what actually lands with buyers.
 Expert Support on Live Calls 
 You will act as the on-call project and impact expert, joining sales and Customer Success calls to explain projects in depth to prospects and customers when a rep needs the specialist in the room.
 You will handle the questions reps can't: permanence and additionality, survivability and replanting, harvest rotation and end use, monitoring and verification methodology, species and site selection, social impact measurement.
 You will represent veritree credibly in front of sustainability, ESG, and procurement stakeholders, and support diligence when deals require it.
 You will treat every call as a diagnostic. The goal is not to be permanently required on calls — it is to notice what reps couldn't answer and turn that into material and coaching so they can next time.
 You will not own the deal, carry a quota, or run the commercial conversation. The rep owns the deal; you make the rep formidable.
 Project & Product Launch 
 You will own the launch checklist and cross-functional readiness for new projects and new solutions — the definition of "ready to sell" and the gate that enforces it.
 You will own each project's availability, not just its launch — taking it online when it's ready and offline when it's sold out or paused.
 You will coordinate Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success through launch, so readiness is planned rather than scrambled.
 You will own the internal communication of what's new: what changed, what it means commercially, and what each team needs to do about it.
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 You will sit at the seam between Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success, and you will be the person all of them come to for the truth about a project.
 You will feed field and buyer insight back to Forest and Product, influencing which projects we source, how we describe them, and what our technology needs to capture next.
 Requirements 
 Professional Requirements
 Exceptional storytelling and writing ability. This is the core of the role. You can hold a room, and you can put the same idea on a page without it going flat. We will ask for writing samples and we will read them closely.
 5-8+ years in product marketing, brand or content strategy, communications, or a comparable narrative-led role. Adjacent backgrounds are welcome — journalism, documentary, impact communications, science communication — if you can show the commercial application.
 A track record of packaging complex or technical subject matter into positioning, narratives, and assets that a sales team actually adopted — with evidence of adoption, not just delivery.
 Demonstrated sales enablement experience — building playbooks, proof-point libraries, and training programs, and measuring whether they changed rep behaviour.
 Comfort being customer-facing as the subject-matter expert: you can present with authority to an enterprise audience and hold up under informed questioning, without needing to run the commercial conversation.
 Genuine appetite for technical and scientific subject matter, and the discipline to represent it accurately. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one. You do not need a forestry background — you need to be the kind of person who will go and learn it properly.
 Experience owning cross-functional process — launch checklists, readiness gates, intake-to-market workflows — in an environment where that process didn't exist yet.
 Fluency with CRM and enablement tooling (HubSpot preferred) and a builder's instinct for using AI to make knowledge accessible at the point of need.
 Based in or able to work core hours in the PST time zone, and willing to travel to customer sites, planting sites, and the Vancouver office as required.
 Personal Strengths
 A storyteller by instinct — you notice the specific detail that makes an abstract claim land, and you reach for it before the statistic.
 A builder who is comfortable creating structure, systems, and process where none exists.
 Genuinely curious about the substance — the forestry, the science, the communities — not just the pitch.
 Mission-driven, with real conviction about restoration done credibly and a low tolerance for greenwashing.
 Rigorous and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know which details matter to a buyer and which don't.
 Influences without authority: you can get Forest, Product, Marketing, and Sales moving in the same direction without owning any of them.
 Clear, direct, and calm under pressure — tech-forward and credible, never cliché.
 Nice to Haves (not mandatory)
 Experience in tree planting, forestry, carbon markets, sustainability, or nature-based solutions.
 Familiarity with ESG and nature reporting frameworks (CSRD, TNFD, SBTi, CDP).
 Experience with MRV (measurement, reporting, and verification) methodologies, remote sensing, or field data collection technology.
 Background in social impact measurement or community development.
 Experience building AI-assisted knowledge bases or enablement tooling for live call support.
 Benefits 
 Why This Role
 You will own the story of what veritree actually sells — and at a company whose entire premise is verified impact, that story is the product. It is a rare brief: real material to work with, twenty-plus projects and the people and ecosystems inside them, plus the data to prove every word of it. You will have the autonomy to build a function that doesn't exist yet, the access to go deep on projects most people only ever see as a line item, and the mandate to make sure the way we sell restoration is as rigorous as the way we deliver it.
 Benefits & Compensation Overview
 Some highlights you can expect include:
 Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth.
 Extended health, dental, and vision benefits.
 Employee discount with tentree, our sister company.

 About the team 
 Risk Engineering builds the systems that protect Stripe from fraud, credit losses, and regulatory risk across user onboarding, compliance, financial crimes, and identity verification.
 Financial Crimes Engineering builds the systems and controls that let Stripe safely onboard businesses in emerging and regulated industries while keeping Stripe in compliance with sanctions law, anti-money-laundering rules, and financial partner requirements. We keep known bad actors off Stripe, find new through ongoing detection, and build AI-augmented tooling that helps expert reviewers resolve cases quickly and accurately.

 As a Staff Engineer on Financial Crimes Engineering, you'll own technical direction across our screening, detection, and review systems. You'll design infrastructure that balances screening latency with accuracy, build the systems that surface emerging risk and collect information to resolve it, and ensure investigators have the tooling they need. You'll work across distributed systems and policy logic, partnering with ML, Legal, and Compliance to translate regulation into working software.

 Define technical strategy & vision: Establish the multi-year architecture for Stripe’s real-time entity matching infrastructure, policy enforcement engines, and reviewer tooling
 Architect high-scale systems: Design and optimize distributed screening engines and detection pipelines handling entity- and transaction-level requests at scale with strict SLA and uptime guarantees.
 Build investigations infrastructure: Design the systems that surface suspicious activity, collect additional information from users, route cases to reviewers, and augment human judgment with AI to drive faster, more accurate case resolution.
 Drive cross-functional technical alignment: Serve as the primary technical voice with Legal, Compliance, ML, and Product leaders to translate evolving global regulatory requirements into technical ones.
 Enable Risk as a Service: Lead the architectural evolution toward a multi-tenant screening platform - laying the technical foundation for both internal product launches and external developer-facing APIs.
 Raise the engineering bar: Set standards for system design, API consistency, and operational rigor across backend and ML-adjacent systems; mentor senior engineers and lead high-stakes design reviews.

WHO ARE WE?

WHY THIS ROLE?

This role is for a highly experienced Back-End Software Engineer who wants to work on core systems that shape how the platform (Model Vault) operates. You will help define the architecture of the platform where reliability, security, performance, and simplicity all matter, and where many of the problems do not have off-the-shelf solutions.

Model Vault is Cohere’s inference platform for deploying and operating models securely at enterprise scale. The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing. We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world’s most demanding enterprise workloads.

AS A SENIOR/STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:

 - Evolve and scale the backend systems that power Model Vault, including authentication and authorization, deployment management, billing, metering, and customer lifecycle.

 - Lead major architectural initiatives across identity, payments, usage systems, platform scalability, and other core product foundations.

 - Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.

 - Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

 - Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.

 - Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.

 - Drive projects end-to-end, from architecture and threat modeling through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration based on real customer workloads.

YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You are a strong backend engineer with excellent fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, networking, operating systems, and security.

 - You have strong programming fundamentals and experience building production systems in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, or similar. You write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and make thoughtful tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and correctness.

 - You have designed and operated production systems where correctness, availability, security, and performance mattered at significant scale.

 - You can take ambiguous, high-impact technical problems, define the right architecture, and drive them through to reliable production systems.

 - You have strong systems-design instincts and understand concepts such as concurrency, consistency, caching, queues, rate limiting, backpressure, failure domains, idempotency, and graceful degradation.

 - You think deeply about security boundaries and understand authentication, authorization, identity, cryptography, secrets, tenant isolation, and how small implementation choices can create significant security risks.

 - You are comfortable reasoning across backend services, APIs, databases, distributed systems, and the cloud infrastructure they run on.

 - You are comfortable diving into unfamiliar codebases and debugging complex problems that cross service or system boundaries.

 - You care about the details of production engineering, including instrumentation, capacity planning, migrations, backwards compatibility, incident response, and safe rollouts.

 - You are comfortable challenging existing architecture and evolving foundational components when the system’s needs change.

 - You have a track record of taking technically difficult projects from an unclear starting point to systems that other engineers and customers depend on.

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.
We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.
 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.
 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.
 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards
 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.
 Professional Experience 
 8+ years of experience across nonprofit fundraising/development, development strategy and/or development operations, including at least 5 years working directly within nonprofit or philanthropic fundraising. Candidates must demonstrate a deep practical understanding of the fundraising cycle, funder decision-making, proposal development and stewardship.
 Strong track record leading the development of complex philanthropic/grant proposals, ideally involving multiple programmes, geographies or internal stakeholders.
 Demonstrated experience turning frontline or field-level input into strategy and prioritization. 
 Demonstrated people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, setting priorities and allocating team capacity. Experience leading a distributed team is strongly preferred.
 Experience operating in a global or matrix organisation, with demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate country leaders, programme teams and other stakeholders who do not report directly to them.
 Comfortable using CRM and pipeline data to support fundraising decisions, forecasting and team management.
 Familiarity with the climate, clean energy, or entrepreneurship support landscape is a strong plus.
 Experience conducting dedicated funder-market or landscape research is advantageous.
 Personal Attributes 
 Structured, analytical thinker who is comfortable synthesizing messy, qualitative field input into clear recommendations.
 High level of adaptability in an environment with evolving team structures and workflows, with a genuine comfort operating in ambiguity - this means being a self-starter and embodying a growth mindset.
 High emotional intelligence — able to lead and support a development team well, build trust with country leads across diverse cultural contexts, and approach unfamiliar markets and norms with genuine curiosity and cultural sensitivity.
 Exceptional written communication skills — able to distill complex, multi-market fundraising intelligence into concise strategy and proposals.
 Strong project management skills; able to run a coordination function across concurrent proposals, deadlines, and stakeholders.
 Comfortable being an internal partner and "connective tissue" role rather than the primary external face of fundraising.
 Ability to work with a global team across time zones, with periodic travel for internal team meetings and relevant conferences/convenings.
 Proficiency in database/CRM management, Google Workspace, and Slack.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Foundational knowledge of global clean energy and climate change solutions and ecosystems and willingness to engage in in-depth self-learning on any gaps.
 Experience building or adding structure to a development operations function from an earlier, more informal stage.

 BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION

About Flinks 
 The Role
 We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks . You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.
 If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.
 What You'll Do
 Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
 Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
 Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
 Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them .
 Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
 Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).
 What You'll Work On
 You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.
 Key areas of focus include:
 Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data. 
 Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams. 
 Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products. 
 Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads. 
 Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery. 
 Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.
 Our stack
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery and dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana and GCP Logging 
 You don't need experience with every tool listed above - strong Data Engineering fundamentals and experience building production data platforms matter more than direct experience with our exact stack. SQL is the exception : it's a non-negotiable (see Key Requirements). 
 Why This Role
 Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products. 
 High leverage impact — your work enables Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Risk teams to move faster with reliable, trusted data. 
 Real-world scale and complexity — work with large volumes of financial data powering products used by banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across North America. 
 Modern cloud-native environment — build on a modern GCP stack using contemporary data, platform, and machine learning tooling.

 Experience: 5+ years of hands-on Data Engineering experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms, pipelines, and warehouse solutions in a cloud environment.

 Cloud Data Platforms: Experience working with modern cloud-native data ecosystems, including data warehouses, event-driven architectures, distributed processing, and platform observability.
 Operational Excellence: Demonstrated ownership of production systems, including monitoring, reliability, performance tuning, cost optimization, incident response, and ongoing platform improvements.
 Machine Learning Platform Exposure: Experience supporting machine learning workflows, feature pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or MLOps environments is an asset, but a strong Data Engineering foundation is the primary requirement.
 Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Data Science, Product, Engineering, and QA teams to deliver trusted, scalable, and well-governed data solutions.
 Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 À propos de Flinks 🚀
 Flinks est une plateforme de finance intégrée qui réunit la connectivité, l’intelligence financière et les paiements, offrant aux entreprises l’infrastructure nécessaire pour concevoir et déployer des expériences financières fluides à grande échelle.
 Chef de file de la finance ouverte (Open Finance) au Canada, nous avons connu une croissance soutenue depuis 2016 pour devenir l’une des plateformes les plus fiables en Amérique du Nord en matière d’accès aux données financières, d’enrichissement des données et de mouvement de fonds. Nous collaborons avec des entreprises innovantes dans de nombreux secteurs, notamment le crédit, les technologies financières (fintech), les services bancaires, l’assurance et la gestion de patrimoine.
 Aujourd’hui, notre plateforme est connectée à plus de 15 000 institutions financières à travers l’Amérique du Nord et soutient plus d’un million de connexions mensuelles. Nous offrons également à nos clients un accès à plus de 4 500 indicateurs financiers en temps réel afin de favoriser une prise de décision plus éclairée. Les entreprises s’appuient sur Flinks pour simplifier l’intégration de leurs utilisateurs, vérifier les revenus, évaluer le risque de crédit et offrir des expériences de paiement plus rapides.

 Nous recrutons notre Ingénieur(e) principal(e) en données (Plateforme Données / IA) afin d’établir l’ingénierie des données comme une discipline à part entière chez Flinks. Vous serez responsable de la plateforme de données et d’apprentissage automatique qui transforme les modèles en services de production fiables, renforcerez les modèles de données sur lesquels l’entreprise s’appuie et assurerez la connexion entre nos scientifiques des données et les équipes produit.
 Il s’agit d’un rôle à forte autonomie, orienté vers la création de nouvelles fondations : une grande partie de cette infrastructure sera à concevoir, bâtir et faire évoluer par vous, plutôt qu’à hériter d’un environnement existant.
 Si vous aimez être la personne qui rend les données et l’IA prêtes pour la production — pipelines, mise en service des modèles, gouvernance, fiabilité — et que vous souhaitez avoir un impact important sur l’ensemble des capacités de données d’une entreprise, ce rôle est fait pour vous.
 Ce que vous ferez
 Assurer la propriété et l’évolution de la plateforme de données — l’entrepôt BigQuery, les couches de transformation dbt, l’orchestration Airflow / Cloud Composer et les mécanismes d’ingestion Pub/Sub qui alimentent chaque modèle et indicateur. 
 Concevoir, exploiter et faire évoluer la plateforme d’apprentissage automatique — pipelines d’entraînement (Kubeflow sur Vertex AI), mise en service des modèles (FastAPI derrière les points de terminaison Vertex), CI/CD, conteneurisation et contrats typés. Assumer la responsabilité opérationnelle de l’infrastructure de mise en production des modèles afin que leur fiabilité ne repose pas uniquement sur les scientifiques des données. 
 Renforcer et standardiser les modèles de données essentiels aux opérations de l’entreprise — amélioration des schémas, correction des problèmes de qualité des données et mise en place de sources de vérité fiables. 
 Mettre en place des pratiques de gouvernance et d’observabilité des données — intégrer sous une gouvernance appropriée les données qui se trouvent à l’extérieur de l’entrepôt et créer des métriques opérationnelles pour les produits qui n’en disposent pas encore. 
 Standardiser les pratiques d’ingénierie des données à travers les différentes lignes de produits — modèles, outils et pipelines pouvant être réutilisés par les autres équipes. 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de science des données, de développement backend et de produit afin de définir et maintenir le contrat entre producteurs et consommateurs de données (modèles produits par la science des données, consommés ou agrégés en aval et exposés aux clients).
 Ce sur quoi vous travaillerez
 Vous contribuerez à bâtir et à faire évoluer la plateforme de données qui alimente les produits d’intelligence financière de Flinks, soutenant notamment l’enrichissement et la catégorisation des transactions, ainsi que les solutions de gestion du risque et de prise de décision liées aux paiements.

 Améliorer la qualité des données, l’observabilité et les indicateurs opérationnels à travers notre plateforme et nos produits destinés aux clients. 
 Développer des services et infrastructures de données performants et optimisés en coûts afin de soutenir des charges de travail en temps réel et par lots. 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit et Ingénierie afin de permettre le développement de nouvelles capacités et d’accélérer la livraison de produits. 
 Contribuer à l’évolution de l’architecture de notre plateforme de données alors que nous continuons à faire croître nos produits, notre clientèle et nos capacités d’apprentissage automatique.
 Notre environnement technologique
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery et dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub et Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow et FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform et Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana et GCP Logging
